name: Hostinger VPS

modes.label: Regular price, 24-month prepaid (amortized monthly)
modes.note: Estimator-only encoding: sizes.hour and month_cap both equal full monthly rent, with a one-hour synthetic minimum. This is NOT a vendor hourly tariff. For valid workloads with sessions >= peak concurrency it charges one monthly rental per concurrent machine, including off-hours. Setup/term cash outlays are caveated separately.

modes.label: Intro price, 24-month prepaid (renews at regular price, e.g. KVM 4 $12.99 -> $28.99)
modes.note: Estimator-only encoding: sizes.hour and month_cap both equal full monthly rent, with a one-hour synthetic minimum. This is NOT a vendor hourly tariff. For valid workloads with sessions >= peak concurrency it charges one monthly rental per concurrent machine, including off-hours. Setup/term cash outlays are caveated separately. hostinger.com/vps-hosting 2026-09-28: "Renews at $28.99/mo for 2 years" (KVM 4); KVM 1/2/8 renew at $11.99/$14.99/$49.99. No promo end date published.

modes.label: 1-month term, no commitment (auto-renews monthly)
modes.note: Same estimator encoding as the 24m modes (hour = month_cap = monthly rent). Steady-state monthly price; first month is discounted to $9.99/$13.99/$25.99/$50.99 (KVM 1/2/4/8). This is the only self-serve option without a 12- or 24-month prepay.

modes.label: Regular price, 12-month prepaid
modes.note: Intro 12-month price (first term only): $6.99/$9.99/$14.99/$28.49 per month (KVM 1/2/4/8), e.g. KVM 4 $179.88 upfront.

modes.label: Hostinger GPU instance (hourly credits, "from" price)
modes.note: hostinger.com/gpu-hosting (2026-09-29) "from" prices = smallest instance size; CPU/RAM/disk chosen at deploy raise the hourly price (size table not published), so these are floors. Billed per started hour from deploy until the instance is deleted, idle or not ("1 hour and 1 second = 2 hours"); no stop/pause, only reboot/destroy; destroyed at zero credit balance; ephemeral storage, no backups; credits non-refundable. Support KB calls the product beta.

plans.name: Usage account
plans.note: Account quotas and stock availability must be checked before deploying 50 concurrent machines; no quota approval implied.

caveats: DIY infrastructure rather than an agent-managed sandbox: guest installation, HTTPS/domain setup, abuse controls and operations are customer responsibilities. Linux guest administrative capabilities are not preinstalled agent features. 30% guest CPU utilization does not reduce allocated-compute charges. Unknowns remain null; a partial subtotal is not a complete invoice.
Smallest captured >=4/8 shape is KVM4: 4vCPU/16GB/200GB; $12.99/month intro, $28.99/month renewal, both paid24months. 8GB KVM2 has only2vCPU and cannot satisfy4vCPU.
KVM4 upfront per machine $311.76 intro or $695.76 renewal; 50-machine cash outlay $15588 or $34788, not $649.50/$1449.50 total cash.
4/8/16/32TB transfer per KVM1/2/4/8 respectively. OneIPv4+IPv6 included; overage price not verified, so not assumed zero.
Snapshot zero is only within included product allowance, not proof of unlimited external50GB retention. Public API exists; no per-hour burst billing or cost-saving power-off.
Free snapshot field represents included product allowance only; no assumption that any quantity/lifetime of requested retained state is supported.

Sustained high CPU is throttled: Hostinger treats a VPS with long sustained high CPU as potentially compromised and cuts its CPU capacity by 25% per hour; the limit can be reset once per week. CPU-bound 24/7 fleets may not get the full vCPU they pay for.

Hostinger API is rate-limited to 90 requests per 60 s per token (RateLimit-Policy q=90;w=60); repeated 429s can get the IP temporarily blocked. VM creation via API is a purchase (POST /api/vps/v1/virtual-machines charges the default payment method). No published limit on the number of VPS per account.
Refunds: 30-day money-back covers new KVM VPS purchases and renewals, but VPS upgrades, VPS control-panel licences, Hostinger GPU and credits are non-refundable.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: A snapshot allows you to capture the entire state of your VPS at a precise moment. You must generate these manually.
snapshot_auto.note: No stop/idle-triggered save; no pause/sleep. Scheduled backups instead: weekly by default (daily is a paid add-on), 'Up to four are retained, two daily and two weekly', restore in place via hPanel or API.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A manual, on-demand capture of your entire VPS
snapshot_on_demand.note: hPanel or API (POST /api/vps/v1/virtual-machines/{id}/snapshot, .../snapshot/restore). Only ONE per VPS ('Creating new snapshot will overwrite the existing snapshot!'), 'Snapshots are automatically deleted after 1 day', deleted on OS reinstall or backup restore. Restore is in place to the same VPS only; no documented boot of new VPS from it (no fork/template). Memory inclusion not documented (disk assumed).

harness_api.quote: Every endpoint is documented under Endpoints, grouped by product — hosting, domains, DNS, email, VPS, WordPress, ecommerce, and billing.
harness_api.note: The public API/CLI/SDK/MCP-server surface covers VM lifecycle, firewall, snapshots/backups, SSH keys and the Docker Manager; none of the documented endpoint groups drive a coding-agent harness (prompt/stream/follow-up).

egress_allowlist.quote: With Hostinger VPS Firewall, packet filtering occurs before incoming traffic reaches the protected server, significantly reducing resource usage.
egress_allowlist.note: Managed firewall is inbound-only: API rule schema has only protocol, port, source ('any'/'custom') and source_detail (IP/CIDR/range), no direction or destination. Outbound filtering only via OS firewall (UFW/iptables) inside the VM, which root can undo.

egress_http_rules.note: No provider-side egress controls at all (see egress_allowlist).

ingress_rules.quote: By default, Hostinger VPS Firewall drops all traffic, which means you must add accept rules for all ports you want to use.
ingress_rules.note: Cloud firewall groups in hPanel and API (/api/vps/v1/firewall...): accept/drop rules by protocol (TCP/UDP/ICMP/GRE/ESP/AH, presets SSH/HTTP/HTTPS/MySQL/PostgreSQL), port or range, source IP/CIDR/range; IPv4 and IPv6; one group can be applied to many VPS; changes apply in <=2 min. Firewall only takes effect once activated on a VPS.

guest_firewall.quote: OS firewalls allow finer rule customization, such as ICMP message handling. If your use case requires this customization, you must still use the OS firewall and Hostinger VPS Firewall.
guest_firewall.note: KVM VM with full root; Hostinger's firewall article points to UFW and iptables tutorials for manual setup, and hPanel has a 'Reset firewall configuration' option for lock-outs.

secret_proxy.quote: While you manage the software environment, Hostinger provides the infrastructure and AI-driven tools to assist you in every step.
secret_proxy.note: No secret-injection proxy is documented anywhere (API reference, Docker Manager, support docs); on a self-managed VPS secrets are just files/env vars you place on the machine yourself.

volume_attach.quote: Individual resources (such as disk space or RAM) can’t be upgraded separately — upgrading the entire VPS plan is required
volume_attach.note: No block/network volume product; disk grows only by plan upgrade (KVM1-8 50-400 GB NVMe).

volume_shared.quote: Individual resources (such as disk space or RAM) can’t be upgraded separately — upgrading the entire VPS plan is required
volume_shared.note: There is no block/network-volume product at all (disk is baked into the plan tier, 50-400 GB NVMe), so there is nothing that could be mounted by multiple running machines at once.

isolation.quote: KVM 1 / KVM 2 / KVM 4 / KVM 8 ... AMD EPYC processors
isolation.note: Hostinger's VPS line is branded 'KVM 1/2/4/8', i.e. full KVM virtual machines, not containers or microVMs.

image_oci.quote: os-templates / get-templates, get-template-details ... virtual-machine / purchase-new-virtual-machine, recreate-virtual-machine
image_oci.note: Machines are provisioned from a fixed catalog of OS/app templates (Linux distros, Docker Manager for compose projects) via the API; there is no endpoint or UI to boot a VM directly from a customer-supplied Docker/OCI image as the root filesystem. Docker/containers run only inside the VM's own OS (docker_inside=true), which is a different feature.

anti_bot.quote: Choose your VPS hosting plan ... KVM virtual machines with root access, dedicated resources, and a public API
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (generic Linux VPS, not a browser/scraping product)

captcha_solving.quote: Choose your VPS hosting plan ... KVM virtual machines with root access, dedicated resources, and a public API
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (generic Linux VPS, not a browser/scraping product)

egress_ip_type.quote: every KVM VPS client gets a dedicated IP address
egress_ip_type.note: Standard datacenter IPv4/IPv6 assigned per VM from Hostinger's own data centers; not residential/mobile.

fork.note: API only supports restoring a snapshot/backup onto the SAME VPS in place; there is no endpoint to clone a VM (running or stopped) into a new independent machine.

fork_running.note: No clone capability at all (see fork), so cloning a running machine without stopping it is not available.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: A snapshot allows you to capture the entire state of your VPS at a precise moment.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Snapshots are disk-state captures restored in place to the same VPS; there is no fork/clone feature at all, so memory-included forking does not exist.

wake_on_request.quote: Choose your VPS hosting plan ... 24/7 live monitoring
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (an always-on VPS you start/stop yourself, not a request-driven serverless sandbox)

auto_stop_idle.quote: Choose your VPS hosting plan ... 24/7 live monitoring
auto_stop_idle.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; billed and running continuously regardless of activity (see also the CPU-throttling-for-sustained-load caveat in the card, which implies no idle auto-stop).

live_resize.quote: The upgrade can take up to 10 minutes to complete.
live_resize.note: Resizing (vCPU/RAM/disk) requires purchasing/switching a whole new plan tier and a ~10-minute migration, not a live in-place resize of the running machine; card's volume_attach evidence also quotes 'Individual resources ... can't be upgraded separately — upgrading the entire VPS plan is required.'

own_agent_api.quote: Hostinger Agent ... Ready-to-use AI team for daily business tasks
own_agent_api.note: Hostinger Agent is a chat-based support/business assistant embedded in hPanel (choose plans, write content, migrate sites, SEO); there is no first-party API to drive it programmatically as a browser/computer-use/research agent.

mcp_server.quote: MCP server — the @hostinger/mcp npm package exposes the API as 372 Model Context Protocol tools for any AI assistant, or connect to the hosted remote server at https://mcp.hostinger.com with no install
mcp_server.note: Covers the full Hostinger API including VPS lifecycle (create/start/stop/snapshot/firewall/etc.), not just the AI chat product.

lang_python.note: Linux VPS with root; Python ships with virtually all listed Linux distro templates, and one-click app templates (Anaconda, Django) provide a ready Python/data-science stack out of the box.

lang_node.note: One-click VPS templates (MEAN/MERN/MEVN stacks, Node-RED) deploy Node.js pre-installed and configured on the VPS out of the box.

static_egress_ip.quote: every KVM VPS client gets a dedicated IP address
static_egress_ip.note: The dedicated IPv4 assigned to the VM is also its outbound/egress address; it stays fixed for the life of the VPS.

windows.quote: Deploy popular Linux operating systems, control panels, and applications on your VPS.
windows.note: OS template catalog is Linux-only (AlmaLinux, Debian, Ubuntu, CentOS, Fedora, Rocky, openSUSE, Arch, Kali, NixOS, Alpine, etc.); no Windows Server template or page exists on the site.

max_session_h.quote: every KVM VPS client gets a dedicated IP address ... 24/7 live monitoring
max_session_h.note: It is a rented VM billed monthly that runs continuously until the customer stops/destroys it or fails to pay; no maximum session/runtime limit is imposed by the provider (separate from the beta hourly-credit GPU product, which is billed differently but still has no fixed session cap).

pause_resume.quote: Hostinger VPS grants you full administrative control and dedicated resources like its own operating system, RAM and CPU.
pause_resume.note: VPS is a fixed-rent subscription VM (monthly/12/24-month prepaid, 'Renews at $X/mo... Cancel anytime'), not usage-metered; resources are dedicated/always-allocated. No Hostinger doc describes a managed pause action that suspends or reduces billing (only OS-level start/stop you perform yourself); the separate GPU-instance product explicitly states 'no stop/pause, only reboot/destroy'. No evidence found of pause/resume for the core KVM VPS either.

nested_virt.quote: Nested virtualization is not supported on Hostinger VPS hosting plans.
nested_virt.note: Direct, unambiguous statement on an official support article dedicated to this exact question.

desktop.quote: Ubuntu 24.04, with a desktop environment, can be accessed remotely using VNC (Virtual Network Computing). VNC allows users to connect to their VPS from any operating system, providing a graphical interface similar to what you would experience if you were sitting in front of the machine.
desktop.note: Hostinger ships a first-party 'Ubuntu 24.04 with Remote Desktop' OS template (VPS > OS & Panel > Change OS > Application > Remote Desktop), requiring KVM 2 or higher, that gives a graphical desktop reachable over VNC out of the box. Corrects the card's false to true.

browser.quote: Ubuntu 24.04 with Remote Desktop template requires a KVM 2 plan or higher
browser.note: The Remote Desktop template documentation covers installing/setting up VNC access and users, but nowhere documents a preinstalled or managed browser as a supported feature; any browser must be installed by the customer like any other software on a self-managed VM. Not offered as a first-party feature.

computer_use.quote: As our VPS solutions are self-managed, you will get full freedom to configure and manage the virtual server.
computer_use.note: Hostinger VPS is a general-purpose self-managed VM product; there is no API to drive a desktop via screenshots/clicks anywhere in the docs or API reference. Not offered: outside the product's scope.

inbound_https.quote: Secure your Hostinger VPS domains using free Let’s Encrypt, Traefik, or custom SSL certificates.
inbound_https.note: HTTPS is entirely do-it-yourself: the customer must deploy Traefik from the Docker catalog or run Certbot manually to terminate TLS. Hostinger does not hand out a managed HTTPS URL to reach ports on the VM.

agent_harnesses.quote: Fully customizable setup: Install dependencies, manage APIs, and configure environments your way — with full root access and snapshots.
agent_harnesses.note: 'Claude Code hosting' / 'Codex Cli Hosting' are generic programmatic SEO landing pages selling the same plain KVM VPS plans; the copy itself says you install and configure the harness yourself. The real Docker application catalog (86 AI/ML one-click apps, checked at hostinger-docker-catalog-applications) lists agent frameworks like Agent Zero, Dify, Flowise, Hermes Agent and OpenClaw, but not Claude Code, Codex CLI, or OpenCode as preinstalled templates.

macos.quote: An OS template is a pre-configured disk image that allows you to install a Linux distribution and specific software stacks instantly. Hostinger offers clean OS installations, templates with pre-installed control panels, and specialized environments for Docker containers... All available Hostinger VPS operating systems are 64bit.
macos.note: The entire VPS OS-template catalog is Linux distributions (Ubuntu, AlmaLinux, Debian, etc.) on AMD EPYC x86-64 KVM hardware; no macOS option exists or is legally offered on this virtualization stack.

arm64.quote: AMD EPYC CPUs, NVMe SSDs, Docker, and full root access
arm64.note: Every KVM plan tier is marketed and built on AMD EPYC (x86-64) processors; no ARM/aarch64 instance type is offered.

self_host.quote: Cloud self-hosting (Hostinger VPS): A professional solution where Hostinger maintains the physical hardware and ensures high uptime in a data center. While you handle the internal software with support from the available AI tools, you do not need to manage the physical and connectivity aspects.
self_host.note: The product itself (the Hostinger VPS platform) runs only in Hostinger's own data centers; a customer manages guest software, not the underlying platform, and cannot run 'Hostinger VPS' on their own infrastructure. Not offered: outside the product's scope.

byoc.quote: Connect globally with local performance. We have data centers in Asia, Europe, North America, and South America. Choose a server close to your location for smoother, faster remote access anywhere in the world.
byoc.note: Machines are only deployed in Hostinger's own listed data-center regions; there is no option to have Hostinger's managed service deployed into a customer's own cloud account. Not offered: outside the product's scope.

open_source.quote: Hostinger provides the infrastructure and AI-driven tools to assist you in every step.
open_source.note: Hostinger is a proprietary commercial hosting company; its VPS platform, hPanel, Docker Manager and API are closed-source products, not released under an OSI license. Not offered: outside the product's scope.

soc2.quote: requires key suppliers to maintain recognized security certifications such as ISO/IEC 27001 or SOC 2 Type II.
soc2.note: Hostinger's public Trust Center (SafeBase/Drata-backed) lists its own achieved certifications as ISO/IEC 27001:2022, PCI DSS v4.0.1, and GDPR compliance; SOC 2 is mentioned only as a requirement it imposes on its own suppliers, not as Hostinger's own attestation. No SOC 2 report, badge, or NDA-gated SOC 2 section exists on the Trust Center.

hipaa.note: The Trust Center's certifications/compliance section lists ISO 27001, PCI DSS, and GDPR only; there is no mention of HIPAA eligibility or a BAA anywhere on the Trust Center or the VPS/GPU product pages. Generic self-managed consumer/SMB VPS product with no healthcare-compliance offering documented.

sso.quote: The customers can authenticate via secure login (username/password) or SSO, with optional 2FA for added protection.
sso.note: Customer-facing SSO login to the Hostinger account/hPanel is explicitly documented on the Trust Center under 'SSO Support'.

usage_api.quote: Every endpoint is documented under Endpoints, grouped by product — hosting, domains, DNS, email, VPS, WordPress, ecommerce, and billing. The API allows 90 requests per minute...VPS creation via API is a purchase.
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: no; The Hostinger API has a billing endpoint group and can create/destroy VPS instances (which trigger purchases), but no documented endpoint exists to query billable usage for a specific sandbox or group of sandboxes by tag/label/project. Hostinger VPS uses fixed monthly subscription pricing per machine, not usage-based metering. Machines are billed continuously at the chosen tier rate regardless of activity or idle state.

locations_quote: Connect globally with local performance. We have data centers in Asia, Europe, North America, and South America. Choose a server close to your location for smoother, faster remote access anywhere in the world.
